t.7.56.1: Having spoken thus to Kākutstha and praised him again and again, Raghunandana then spoke yet another speech.
t.7.56.2: Here are four thousand horses, O bull among men, and two thousand chariots, and a hundred elephants as well.
t.7.56.3: O Śatrughna, let the rows of market stalls, adorned with many kinds of wares, follow you, and likewise the actors and dancers.
t.7.56.4: Take ten thousand pieces of gold and fine gold, O bull among men, and go, Śatrughna, well provided with wealth and mounts.
t.7.56.5: And, O hero, this unsurpassed army, well maintained, cheerful and well fed, you should address with kind words and gladden with gifts, O best of men.
t.7.56.7: Therefore, having sent ahead a great army thronged with joyful men, go you alone, bow in hand, to that forest of Madhu.
t.7.56.6: For neither wealth nor wives nor kinsmen stand by a man so firmly, O Rāghava, as does a well-contented body of servants.
t.7.56.8: You should go in such a way, unsuspected, that Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, does not know that you are coming in search of battle.
t.7.56.9: For there is no other death for him, O bull among men: whoever comes into his sight is surely to be slain by Lavaṇa.
t.7.56.10: When the summer has passed and the rainy season has set in, you should slay Lavaṇa, O gentle one, for that indeed is the time for this evil-minded one.
t.7.56.11: Let your soldiers set out with the great seers at their head, so that they may cross the waters of the Jāhnavī during what remains of the summer.
t.7.56.12: Then, having stationed the whole army on the bank of the river, go on ahead, watchful and composed, with only your bow, O you of swift valour.
t.7.56.13: Thus addressed by Rāma, Śatrughna gathered those mighty chiefs of the army and then spoke these words.
t.7.56.14: These are the dwellings assigned to you, wherever you will reside; and you must live there without conflict, so that there is no harm to anyone.
t.7.56.15: Having thus instructed them and sent forth the great army, he respectfully saluted Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī.
t.7.56.16: Having circumambulated Rāma and bowed low before him with his head, Śatrughna, scorcher of foes, was given leave by Rāma.
t.7.56.17: Śatrughna, self-controlled and mighty, bowed with joined palms to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata and to the family priest Vasiṣṭha; then, having circumambulated them reverently, he departed.
